status: durable owner correction / article remains unregistered
owner_correction: Stop using first-person preference or permission wrappers such as 'I want ...' and 'I don't get to ...' when the sentence is really making a general recommendation or criterion. They sound strange because the reader has no reason to care what the author wants or what the author gets to do.
scope: Joel-byline advice/explanatory prose where the underlying point is a general criterion, boundary, consequence, or recommendation rather than Joel's personal preference itself.
do_not_overgeneralize: This is not a ban on first person or on the word 'want'. First person remains correct for autobiography, actual personal preferences, memories, claims about Joel's experience, and cases where Joel's preference itself is the subject. Source-derived statements such as a child learning that what they wanted did not matter are also unaffected.
preferred_repair: State the criterion or consequence directly. Example: instead of 'I want therapy to leave me more able to stand on my own feet' say directly that a good process should make the helper less necessary over time. Instead of 'I don't actually get to say no' state that treating every disagreement as resistance makes disagreement impossible or folds every answer back into the same theory.
interaction_with_existing_rules: Extends the repository's existing warning against significance-staging 'I want ...' constructions by adding permission/entitlement-style first-person wrappers as the same reader-facing register problem.
current_application: Episode 007 R7 contains no 'I want', 'I get to', 'I don't get to', or 'I need' preference/permission wrapper in the advice passages.
